title: Tile Calculator
description: Calculate exactly how many tiles you need for a floor or wall based on tile size and waste factor.

formula.summary: The area to cover is divided by the area of a single tile, then increased by a waste percentage and rounded up to a whole number of tiles.

variables.meaning: Converts tile dimensions from square inches to square feet
Extra tiles to cover cuts, breakage, and pattern matching

faqs.question: How much waste factor should I use for tile?
faqs.answer: 10% is typical for a straight layout with standard-size tiles. Use 15-20% for diagonal layouts, large-format tiles, or intricate patterns that create more cuts and offcuts.

faqs.question: Should I buy tiles from the same batch?
faqs.answer: Yes - tile color and shade can vary slightly between production batches, so buying all your tiles (including extras) from the same lot number avoids visible mismatches.

seoContent.heading: Calculating tile quantity accurately
seoContent.body: Tile projects are unforgiving of underestimates - running short mid-installation often means waiting on a special order or risking a batch mismatch. This calculator computes the exact area-based tile count and applies a waste factor so you buy enough on the first trip.

seoContent.heading: Tile size and layout complexity
seoContent.body: Larger tiles generally mean fewer total tiles but more waste per cut, since a single mis-cut wastes a bigger, more expensive piece. Complex layouts (diagonal, herringbone, mixed sizes) increase the number of cuts needed, which is why this calculator lets you dial in a custom waste percentage rather than assuming a fixed rate.
